prerequisites.title: Gusto Developer Account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up before filing the Production Pre-Approval application.

prerequisites.title: Security documentation
prerequisites.detail: Gather audits (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS), penetration test reports, policies, and security and incident contacts. Without a formal audit, describe your controls (MFA, encryption, vulnerability scanning).

steps.title: Create Gusto Developer Account
steps.detail: Sign up for a Gusto Developer Account.
steps.done_when: You can log in to the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Prepare security evidence pack
steps.detail: Draft the questionnaire answers and collect policy documents and control descriptions.
steps.done_when: All documents and answers are ready for the application.

steps.title: File Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: Submit the application with the security details and contacts; no further action is needed until Gusto replies.

steps.title: Wait for Partnerships and Security Review
steps.detail: Partnerships reviews first, then the GRC team starts the Security Review. Gusto may ask for more information, which pauses the review.
steps.done_when: Gusto approves the application and review.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for gusto with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Build and test in demo environment
steps.detail: Build against api.gusto-demo.com and test the assigned scopes there.
steps.done_when: The integration works in demo with the assigned scopes.

steps.title: Pass QA and receive production credentials
steps.detail: Complete Gusto's QA; Gusto then issues production credentials in the Developer Portal.
steps.done_when: Production credentials are visible in the Developer Portal.

traps.title: Annual and change-triggered re-review
traps.detail: API access depends on passing annual security reviews. Gusto may also require review after integration changes.

traps.title: No production test accounts
traps.detail: All testing, before and after launch, must happen in the demo environment.

traps.title: Scopes are out of your control
traps.detail: Gusto assigns scopes during review, and out-of-scope calls are rejected in production. Request only the minimum; changes later need an email to Gusto.

traps.title: Rate limit is 200 requests per minute
traps.detail: The limit applies per OAuth grant over a 60-second rolling window; excess requests get HTTP 429.

blockers.what_it_means: Gusto needs more information than the Pre-Approval application provided.
blockers.what_to_do: Respond promptly with the requested documents.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft responses and assemble the supporting documentation.

blockers.what_it_means: The call is outside the scopes assigned to your app.
blockers.what_to_do: Check granted scopes in the Developer Portal and email Gusto to request changes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the API calls your code makes against the granted scopes.

evidence.quote: **Your users see OAuth consent screens.** In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: In production, users should see your app name rather than Composio on consent screens, and this is the most common reason to switch to your own app.

evidence.quote: Developer’s continued access to the Gusto API is contingent upon Developer completing and passing annual security reviews
evidence.answer: Per Gusto's Developer Terms (last updated August 30, 2023), continued API access depends on passing annual security reviews, so reviews repeat yearly.

evidence.question: G6

evidence.answer: Gusto may require extra security reviews when the developer changes the integration, so reviews also repeat on changes (at Gusto's discretion).

evidence.answer: The developer license to use Gusto's Developer Tools is stated as royalty-free; the terms do not mention a paid plan, credits, or fees for API access, and that point is not confirmed by pricing pages I could read.
